info.title: posterProjects Mobile API
info.description: Stateless bearer-token surface at /api/v1, consumed by the posterMobile Flutter client. Tokens are Laravel Sanctum personal access tokens named `mobile` with the `mobile` ability, separate from the web session app and the `/mcp` bearer surface (which uses the `mcp` ability). This document describes the surface as implemented, including the exact JSON error contract.

servers.description: Relative to the application origin. Paths below already include the full /api/v1 prefix.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: Credentials-to-token exchange, identity, and revocation for the mobile bearer surface.

tags.name: Projects
tags.description: Read-only project list and detail for the posterMobile client. Writes are a separate change.

tags.name: Issues
tags.description: Read-only, board-ordered issue list and single-issue detail, nested under a project and addressed by the human key. Writes are a separate change, gated on board-column/sprint discovery.

tags.name: Board Columns
tags.description: Read-only board-column vocabulary for a project, ordered by position. The client composes a full board from this collection plus GET /issues?sprint={id}, grouping issues by board_column_id — there is no nested /board endpoint.

tags.name: Sprints
tags.description: Read-only sprint vocabulary for a project, newest first, each with a server-computed state and an issues_count. The board composes from board-columns + sprints + GET /issues?sprint={id}; the response here is the complete set because an absent meta means data is complete.

tags.name: Labels
tags.description: Read-only label catalogue for a project, ordered by name, each with an eager issues_count. An issue's labels already ride on every issue row, but a zero-issue label is otherwise unreachable in the API; the response here is the complete set because an absent meta means data is complete.

post.summary: Exchange credentials for a mobile bearer token
post.description: Validates the owner's email and password without starting a web session (Auth::validate(), never Auth::attempt()). On success, revokes every prior token named `mobile` before minting a new one named `mobile` with exactly the `mobile` ability. A pre-existing `mcp` token is never touched. Throttled by the named limiter `api-login`: 5 attempts per minute keyed by `email|ip`, and 10 attempts per minute keyed by `ip` alone; both successful and failed attempts count toward each limit.

200.description: Credentials valid. Returns the plain-text token; it is never shown again.

422.description: Missing/invalid fields, or a recognized-but-wrong email/password pair. Bad credentials are reported under the `email` field, reusing the existing Spanish copy.

value.message: Estas credenciales no coinciden con nuestros registros.

email: Estas credenciales no coinciden con nuestros registros.

429.description: 6th attempt within the one-minute window for the same email+IP, or 11th for the same IP.

example.message: Demasiados intentos de acceso. Por favor, inténtalo de nuevo en 42 segundos.

post.summary: Redeem a QR login pass for a mobile bearer token
post.description: Exchanges a short-lived, single-use QR pass (minted by an authenticated browser session at POST settings/mobile-token/qr) for a token byte-identical to POST /api/v1/login's: named `mobile`, ability `['mobile']`. Revokes every prior token named `mobile` before minting the new one; a pre-existing `mcp` token is never touched. Unauthenticated by design — the pass itself is the credential. Consumption is a single conditional UPDATE keyed on `affected === 1`; unknown, expired, already-consumed, and malformed pass values are indistinguishable and all produce the same 422 body (see the api-qr-login spec's 'Uniform Redemption Failure' requirement). Throttled by the named limiter `api-qr-redeem`: 10 attempts per minute keyed by IP alone, since no identity exists before a pass is validated.

200.description: Pass valid, unconsumed, and unexpired. Returns the plain-text token; it is never shown again.

422.description: The pass value is unknown, expired, already consumed, or malformed. All four causes are byte-identical and never disclose which one occurred.

example.message: El código QR no es válido o expiró.

token: El código QR no es válido o expiró.

429.description: 11th redemption attempt from the same IP within one minute.

example.message: Demasiados intentos de acceso. Por favor, inténtalo de nuevo en 42 segundos.

get.description: Requires a bearer token carrying the `mobile` ability (or the legacy wildcard `['*']` ability). Exposes exactly id, name, and email — no other user attribute.

401.description: No token, or a token that does not authenticate.

403.description: A valid token that lacks the `mobile` ability (e.g. an `mcp`-only token).

example.message: Este token no tiene permiso para usar esta API.

get.summary: List the authenticated owner's active projects
get.description: Returns the requesting user's active (non-archived) projects, scoped by membership, ordered by name then id. Requires the `mobile` ability. There is no pagination envelope today: `data` is always the complete result set. Forward-compatibility rule for the client: if a future response omits `meta`, `data` is still the complete set — there is no next page. If `meta` is present, the last page is reached when `meta.current_page === meta.last_page` (equivalently `links.next === null`). A client written against this rule never breaks and never has to assume the response has exactly one key.

200.description: The member's active projects, ordered by name.

401.description: No token, or a token that does not authenticate.

403.description: A valid token that lacks the `mobile` ability (e.g. an `mcp`-only token).

example.message: Este token no tiene permiso para usar esta API.

get.summary: Resolve a single project by key, active or archived
get.description: Resolves `{project}` against the project's `key` column for any project the requesting user is a member of, including a soft-deleted (archived) one — a stale link to an archived project still resolves so the client can render a meaningful state instead of a dead end. Requires the `mobile` ability. Unknown key, non-member key, and force-deleted key are indistinguishable: all three respond `404` with the identical generic body, never `403` — the response never discloses whether an inaccessible key exists.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: The project's `key` (e.g. DEMO) — never the numeric `id`.

401.description: No token, or a token that does not authenticate.

403.description: A valid token that lacks the `mobile` ability (e.g. an `mcp`-only token).

example.message: Este token no tiene permiso para usar esta API.

404.description: No project with this key is resolvable for the requesting user: the key never existed, belongs to a project the user is not a member of, or was permanently force-deleted. These three causes are intentionally indistinguishable.

get.summary: List a project's issues, board-ordered and paginated
get.description: Returns `{project}`'s issues ordered by board column position, then issue position, then issue id as a mandatory tiebreaker (position is unique only within a board-column/sprint scope). Paginated: `per_page` defaults to 50 and is capped at 100 regardless of the requested value; `links.next` retains every applied query filter. `?sprint=` accepts an integer sprint id belonging to `{project}`, or the literal `backlog` for unsprinted issues; absent, every issue in the project is returned. A sprint id belonging to a different project responds `404`; a value that is neither `backlog` nor an integer responds `422`. Requires the `mobile` ability. An archived (soft-deleted) `{project}` responds `404`, unlike `GET /api/v1/projects/{project}`.

parameters.name: sprint
parameters.description: An integer sprint id belonging to `{project}`, or the literal `backlog` for unsprinted issues. Absent returns every issue in the project.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Items per page. Default 50, capped at 100.

get.summary: Resolve a single issue by its human key
get.description: Resolves `{issue}` (e.g. DEMO-123) via `Issue::resolveByKey()` against `{project}`, never route-model binding — `key` is a computed accessor, not a column. Requires the `mobile` ability. Seven distinct causes converge on the identical `404`: an unresolvable `{project}` (unknown key, non-member key, archived project), and a malformed, cross-project, or unknown `{issue}` (no dash, non-numeric/empty suffix, prefix mismatch, unknown number). None is distinguishable from the response.

parameters.description: The project's `key` (e.g. DEMO) — never the numeric `id`.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description: The full issue key (e.g. DEMO-123) — never the numeric `id`.

200.description: The issue, with every relation embedded.

get.summary: List a project's board columns, ordered by position
get.description: Returns the complete, unpaginated set of `{project}`'s board columns ordered by position — no tiebreaker needed, position is unique within a project. An empty column (no issues assigned) is still returned. No query parameter is accepted. Requires the `mobile` ability. An archived (soft-deleted) `{project}` responds `404`, matching `GET /api/v1/projects/{project}/issues`.

get.summary: List a project's sprints, newest first, with computed state
get.description: Returns the complete, unpaginated set of `{project}`'s sprints ordered by start_date descending, id descending as the mandatory tiebreaker (start_date is a date and may repeat). Each sprint carries a server-computed `state` (`future` when start_date is after today, `completed` when end_date is before today, `active` otherwise — both bounds inclusive, anchored to today() in the application timezone, UTC) and an eager `issues_count` aggregate. The client's default sprint is the first element with `state: "active"`, matching the web board's pick for identical data. No query parameter is accepted. Requires the `mobile` ability. An archived (soft-deleted) `{project}` responds `404`, matching `GET /api/v1/projects/{project}/issues`.

get.summary: List a project's label catalogue, ordered by name
get.description: Returns the complete, unpaginated set of `{project}`'s labels ordered by name ascending — no tiebreaker needed, name is unique within a project. A label attached to no issues is still returned, with issues_count: 0 — the row an issue's embedded labels can never surface. issues_count is an eager withCount aggregate, never a per-row query. No query parameter is accepted. Requires the `mobile` ability. An archived (soft-deleted) `{project}` responds `404`, matching `GET /api/v1/projects/{project}/issues`.

Issue.description: The board-card shape: exactly these 15 fields, no more, no fewer.

id.description: Stable local primary key. Never used to address the resource.

number.description: The per-project sequential number, i.e. the suffix of key.

position.description: Order within its board column and sprint scope. Not globally unique.

next.description: Retains every applied query filter (e.g. ?sprint=). Null on the last page.

links.description: Laravel's default presentational page-link list. Ignorable by the client.

IssueChildRef.description: A child issue reference, as it appears on the parent's board-card list.

IssueDetail.description: The full single-issue shape: the 15 `Issue` fields plus description, reporter, parent, children, and comments.

comments.description: Ordered by created_at ascending, with issue id as the tiebreaker for comments sharing a timestamp.

BoardColumn.description: Exactly these 4 fields, no more, no fewer. Deliberately no issues_count: a column's count is meaningless without a sprint filter, since one column holds issues from every sprint at once.

id.description: Stable local primary key. Never used to address the resource.

position.description: Order within the project's board. Unique per project at the database level, so no tiebreaker is needed.

Sprint.description: Exactly these 8 fields, no more, no fewer. state is computed server-side from today() in the application timezone (UTC) — never sent by the client, never a device-clock computation.

id.description: Stable local primary key. Never used to address the resource.

issues_count.description: Eager-loaded aggregate; never triggers a query per sprint.

Label.description: Exactly these 4 fields, no more, no fewer. No color, no project_id (the URL already carries the project), no nested issues.

id.description: Stable local primary key. Never used to address the resource.

issues_count.description: Eager-loaded aggregate (withCount); never triggers a query per label. 0 for a label attached to no issues.
